added_models.model: FIX-knockout and normal mice given scAAV8.FIXR338L (BAX 335 / AskBio009)

engagement.population: Severe or moderately severe hemophilia B (FIX activity ≤2%)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Hum Gene Ther, PMC4326268); PubMed entry Nov 2014, epub 21 Jan 2015.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry: the model is BAX 335's own mouse package, a different system from the draft's AAV8 FIX-Padua dogs.
engagement.model: FIX-knockout and normal mice given scAAV8.FIXR338L (BAX 335 / AskBio009)
engagement.note: BAX 335 vector gave dose-linear FIX activity in hemophilic mice, followed for 8-10 months; preclinical package for the Phase 1/2.
engagement.quote: The scAAV8.FIXR338L vector produced greater than 6-fold increased FIX specific activity compared with wild-type FIX and demonstrated linear dose responses from doses that produced 2-500% FIX activity

engagement.magnitude_basis: sustained FIX activity at 12 months: mice 8-10 months durable vs patients lost by 5-11 weeks in 7 of 8
engagement.population: Severe or moderately severe hemophilia B (FIX activity ≤2%)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; full text (PMC7885820) not retrieved (Europe PMC 500). NCT01687608 has no posted results. Earlier sponsor/ASH disclosures (2015-2016) not checked, so the year may be earlier.
engagement.judgement: The readout moved at peak but the model's durable expression did not hold; scored contra because the mouse predicted sustained expression and the loss (attributed to CpG-driven innate immunity) is something the model did not show. Paired by me: Konkle states no comparison with the mice.
engagement.model: FIX-knockout and normal mice given scAAV8.FIXR338L (BAX 335 / AskBio009)
engagement.note: Peak FIX reached 32-58% at the top dose, but expression was lost within 5-11 weeks in 7 of 8 patients; mice had held it for months.
engagement.quote: One participant achieved sustained therapeutic FIX activity of ∼20%, without bleeding or replacement therapy, for 4 years; in others, FIX activity was not sustained beyond 5 to 11 weeks.

safety.population: Severe or moderately severe hemophilia B (FIX activity ≤2%)
safety.judgement: Opening entry for BAX 335's mouse safety package.
safety.model: FIX-knockout and normal mice given scAAV8.FIXR338L (BAX 335 / AskBio009)
safety.note: Hemophilic mice expressing FIX-Padua at 100-500% for 8-10 months showed no thrombosis and no FIX antibodies.
safety.short: Mice: no thrombosis, no FIX inhibitors
safety.quote: Necropsy of FIX(-/-) mice 8-10 months after vector delivery revealed no microvascular or macrovascular thrombosis in mice expressing FIXR338L (plasma FIX activity, 100-500%).

safety.magnitude_basis: thrombosis and FIX inhibitors: absent in mice and in 8 patients
safety.population: Severe or moderately severe hemophilia B (FIX activity ≤2%)
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; n=8 and patient FIX peaked at 32-58%, far below the mice's tested range, so the thrombosis test is weak.
safety.judgement: Scored same on the harms the mouse could show (thrombosis, FIX antibodies). The loss of expression is scored in engagement, not counted again here.
safety.model: FIX-knockout and normal mice given scAAV8.FIXR338L (BAX 335 / AskBio009)
safety.note: No thrombosis, inhibitors or FIX-Padua immunity in 8 patients, as the mice predicted; patient FIX stayed below the mice's 100-500%.
safety.short: No thrombosis or inhibitors in patients
safety.quote: No clinical thrombosis, inhibitors, or other FIX Padua-directed immunity was reported.

added_models.model: Cynomolgus monkeys with pre-existing anti-AAV5 NABs given AMT-060 (AAV5-hFIX)

engagement.population: AMT-060-treated hemophilia B patients with and without pre-existing anti-AAV5 NABs
engagement.confidence_note: First public use of the NAB-stratified NHP analysis; dosing date of the monkeys not stated in the abstract.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry at the model's first public use; it opens and is scored in the same paper.
engagement.model: Cynomolgus monkeys with pre-existing anti-AAV5 NABs given AMT-060 (AAV5-hFIX)
engagement.note: Monkeys dosed with AMT-060 were stratified by pre-existing anti-AAV5 NAB titer to ask whether NABs block hFIX expression.
engagement.short: NHP: do AAV5 NABs block expression?
engagement.quote: Further studies in non-human primates (NHPs) showed that AAV5 transduction efficacy was similar following AMT-060 treatment, irrespective of the pre-existing anti-AAV5 NABs titers.

engagement.magnitude_basis: hFIX expression despite pre-existing anti-AAV5 NABs: NHP titers up to 1030 vs patient titers up to 340
engagement.population: AMT-060-treated hemophilia B patients with and without pre-existing anti-AAV5 NABs
engagement.confidence_note: Sponsor-authored (uniQure). Full text read (PMC6586596). The NHP analysis is presented after the patient re-testing, so treated as a retrodiction; the prospective use (no NAB exclusion in AMT-061 Phase 2b) is etranacogene, not a member, so it does not score here. registry_date is NCT02396342 results posting.
engagement.judgement: Retro, not same: the patient NAB result (AMT-060, 10 patients) was known when the NHP analysis was reported. Patient-level because it predicts which patients (NAB-positive) still respond.
engagement.model: Cynomolgus monkeys with pre-existing anti-AAV5 NABs given AMT-060 (AAV5-hFIX)
engagement.note: Monkeys reproduced the patient finding: pre-existing anti-AAV5 NABs did not prevent therapeutic hFIX expression.
engagement.quote: We show that therapeutic efficacy of AAV5-mediated gene therapy was achieved in humans with pre-existing anti-AAV5 NABs titers up to 340. Whereas in NHPs circulating human factor IX (hFIX) protein was achieved, at a level therapeutic in humans

added_models.model: Cynomolgus monkeys given AAVRh74var-hFIX-Padua (fidanacogene predecessor), GLP toxicology

safety.population: Severe or moderately severe hemophilia B (FIX activity ≤2%)
safety.confidence_note: model_first_use_year 2015 is a proxy (Phase 1/2a NCT02484092 started Nov 2015); the study was public only in the April 2024 SBRA. Predecessor product differs from Beqvez in a redacted element.
safety.judgement: Separate system from the draft's hemophilia B dog tracks: wild-type monkeys, human FIX-Padua, toxicology study filed with the BLA.
safety.model: Cynomolgus monkeys given AAVRh74var-hFIX-Padua (fidanacogene predecessor), GLP toxicology
safety.note: Monkeys at 2-10x the clinical dose reached FIX activity 2-4x normal without thrombosis; run before the 2015 Phase 1/2a (year is a proxy).
safety.quote: No test article-related adverse findings were observed in this study, including any findings of thrombosis by microscopic histopathology.

safety.magnitude_basis: thromboembolic events: none in NHPs at 2-4x normal FIX; none in Phase 1/2a or Phase 3 patients
safety.population: Severe or moderately severe hemophilia B (FIX activity ≤2%)
safety.confidence_note: Both sides in the same FDA review but in separate sections; the review does not compare them. Patients (64%) had transaminase elevations the NHPs did not show; capsid-directed T-cell hepatitis is not reproduced in monkeys, so its silence is not counted as a miss.
safety.judgement: Scored on thrombosis, the on-target harm of a supraphysiologic gain-of-function FIX that the monkey could show; same, pooled across modalities. The anti-hFIX antibodies in NHPs are a xenogeneic artefact and were not predicted for patients.
safety.model: Cynomolgus monkeys given AAVRh74var-hFIX-Padua (fidanacogene predecessor), GLP toxicology
safety.note: No thromboembolic events or FIX inhibitors in either trial, as the NHP study predicted; NHP silence on transaminase rises is not scored.
safety.short: No thrombosis in patients, as predicted
safety.quote: There were no infusions reactions, malignancy, inhibitors to FIX, thromboembolic events or deaths reported in either trial.

added_models.model: Rhesus macaques given AAVS3-hFIX vectors (FLT180a capsid), with human hepatocyte and FRG humanized-liver mouse transduction

engagement.model: Rhesus macaques given AAVS3-hFIX vectors (FLT180a capsid), with human hepatocyte and FRG humanized-liver mouse transduction
engagement.population: Severe or moderately severe hemophilia B (FIX activity ≤2%)
engagement.confidence_note: ASH 2018 abstract (Blood 132 Suppl 1:2197), read in full on ScienceDirect; 14 macaques, two FIX cassettes, not necessarily the exact FLT180a cassette.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry: FLT180a's own capsid in macaques, a different system from the draft's hemophilic dog tracks.
engagement.note: AAVS3-FIX in macaques gave ~11% of normal hFIX at 0.93e12 vg/kg and ~430% at 2.56e13 vg/kg; preclinical support for the B-AMAZE Phase 1/2.
engagement.quote: AAVS3 FIX vectors injected at clinically relevant doses of 0.93 x1012 to 2.56 x1013 vg/kg achieved mean peak levels of 0.546 and 21.7µg/ml of hFIX respectively (~11% to ~430% of normal levels).

engagement.magnitude_basis: FIX activity: macaques ~11% of normal at 0.93e12 vg/kg vs patients 23-260% (five normal, 51-78%) at 0.38-1.28e12 vg/kg
engagement.model: Rhesus macaques given AAVS3-hFIX vectors (FLT180a capsid), with human hepatocyte and FRG humanized-liver mouse transduction
engagement.population: Severe or moderately severe hemophilia B (FIX activity ≤2%)
engagement.confidence_note: NEJM abstract only (full text paywalled); FIX levels by dose not read, only the pooled range. Chowdary does not compare with the macaques; paired by me.
engagement.judgement: The proximal readout (transgene FIX) rose dose-dependently in patients as the macaques showed, so same; the macaque underpredicted human potency several-fold, as expected for a capsid built for human hepatocytes. Liver enzyme rises needing immunosuppression are capsid T-cell immunity the macaque cannot show, not scored.
engagement.note: All 10 patients had dose-dependent FIX rises; at 0.38-1.28e12 vg/kg levels reached 23-260%, well above the macaques' ~11% near 1e12 vg/kg.
engagement.reason: transgene FIX expressed, higher than predicted
engagement.quote: After receiving the infusion, all the patients had dose-dependent increases in factor IX levels.

safety.confidence_note: model_first_use_year 2015 is a proxy (study run before the Nov 2015 Phase 1/2a, public only in the April 2024 SBRA). Predecessor differs from Beqvez in a redacted element.

safety.magnitude_basis: test-article deaths with brain/skin pathology in mice vs no deaths or thromboembolic events in Phase 1/2a and Phase 3 patients
safety.model: Healthy male mice given AAVRh74var-hFIX-Padua (fidanacogene predecessor), GLP toxicology
safety.population: Severe or moderately severe hemophilia B (FIX activity ≤2%)
safety.confidence_note: Both sides in the same FDA review, separate sections. FDA read the mouse deaths as exacerbated tissue/vascular injury from repeated bleeds in animals with endogenous FIX, so the harm may be a model artefact rather than a prediction.
safety.judgement: Under the brief, a model harm that never appeared in patients is contra with magnitude opposite: the mice signalled lethal vascular/tissue harm at sub-clinical doses, and none occurred in patients.
safety.note: No deaths, thromboembolic events or FIX inhibitors in either trial, unlike the mouse study's test-article deaths.
safety.quote: There were no infusions reactions, malignancy, inhibitors to FIX, thromboembolic events or deaths reported in either trial.
